title: Module 23: Buying and Selling Online Safely

screens.heading: You are safe here
screens.reassurance: This module will not make any purchases or share any payment information. You are just reading.
screens.goal: By the end of this module, you will know how to spot scam messages on online marketplaces, buy safely from strangers, and sell your own items with confidence.

screens.heading: Frank's three messages
body: Frank listed a used lawnmower on Facebook Marketplace for $150. He received three responses the same afternoon.

Message 1: 'I'll take it! I'm sending a courier to pick it up. I'm sending an e-Transfer for $350 to cover the item plus courier fees. Please send back the extra $200.' This is a scam — no real buyer sends more than the asking price.

Message 2: 'I'm interested. Click here to see my offer.' The link was a phishing page designed to steal his email and password. Message 3: 'Is the mower still available? I can pick it up Saturday morning. What is your address?' This was a real buyer. Frank sold the mower and got $150 in cash.
screens.tellMeMore: The 'overpayment scam' (Message 1) works by sending a fake e-Transfer or cheque for more than the asking price, then asking you to send the difference back. The original payment is eventually cancelled or reversed — but the money you sent back is gone. Real buyers never overpay. Real buyers never involve couriers you have to pay.

screens.heading: Spotting a scam buyer or seller
body: Red flags from buyers: offers above your asking price, mentions of shipping or couriers, requests to move the conversation to another platform (WhatsApp, email), sending payment before seeing the item, urgency ('I need it today, please confirm immediately').

Red flags from sellers: price that seems too good to be true, refuses to meet in person or show the item on video, asks for payment in gift cards, e-Transfer, or wire transfer before you have seen the item, newly created account with no history.

The safest rule: for marketplace transactions, cash in person is the safest payment. Meet in a public place (a mall parking lot, a library, a Tim Hortons). Never invite a stranger to your home for a first meeting.
screens.tellMeMore: Many Canadian police stations and major retailers (Canadian Tire, Walmart) now offer 'safe exchange zones' — a designated well-lit area with security cameras where you can safely meet marketplace buyers and sellers. Search 'safe exchange zone [your city]' to find the nearest one.

screens.heading: Buying safely from online marketplaces
body: Check the seller's profile: how long have they been on the platform? Do they have reviews or ratings? A seller with 50 positive reviews and a two-year-old account is far more trustworthy than a new account with no history.
Ask to see the item working (or being shown) before you commit. For electronics, ask the seller to power it on over video call. For a car, request a Carfax report.

For high-value items (furniture, appliances, vehicles): bring a friend or family member to the exchange. Two people are always safer than one. Tell someone where you are going and when you expect to be back.
screens.tellMeMore: Facebook Marketplace, Kijiji, and Craigslist do not screen their listings for fraud. They provide a platform, but the transaction is between you and the stranger. The Consumer Protection Act of Ontario gives you limited recourse for private sales — most 'as-is' sales cannot be returned. Before any significant purchase from a stranger, ask: 'Would I be comfortable if this went wrong?' If the answer is no, walk away.

screens.heading: Selling safely
body: Write an honest, detailed listing with clear photos. Good photos taken in natural light get more responses and attract serious buyers. Price realistically — search for similar items on the platform to see what they sell for.
Never share your home address until you have confirmed the buyer is real and agreed on a meeting time and place. Use a public meeting spot for the exchange.
Accept cash or Interac e-Transfer only. Never accept cheques, money orders, or digital wallets you are not familiar with. If a buyer insists on an unusual payment method, decline.
screens.tellMeMore: If you are selling a device (phone, tablet, computer): factory reset it before the sale to remove all your personal data. On an iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content. On Android: Settings > General Management > Reset > Factory Data Reset. This removes your photos, emails, accounts, and passwords so the new owner starts from scratch.

screens.heading: Online marketplaces are safe when you know the rules
takeaways: Never accept payment above your asking price — it is always a scam.
Cash in person at a public location is the safest marketplace transaction.
Check the other person's account history and reviews before agreeing to a transaction.
Safe exchange zones at police stations and major retailers exist for exactly this purpose.
Factory reset any device before selling it to remove all your personal data.
screens.confidence: You can now buy and sell on online marketplaces safely — recognising the scams before they happen and protecting your money every step of the way.
